examples.name: actions
examples.title: actions — denext Server Actions
examples.blurb: A guestbook demonstrating Server Actions ("use server") two ways.
examples.run:
# from this directory
deno task dev             # http://localhost:3000
deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: animation
examples.title: denext × motion + react-spring
examples.blurb: Two real npm animation libraries — motion (motion.dev) and @react-spring/web — co-existing in one project, both running on denext's single React.
examples.run:
deno task example:animation          # build once, serve
deno task example:animation --dev    # rebuild on each request

examples.name: auth
examples.title: examples/auth — a runnable denextAuth app
examples.blurb: The production shape of denext's first-party auth in one small app, zero npm: Deno's built-in node:sqlite holds everything, and every screen works with JavaScript disabled (tests/auth-example.test.ts…
examples.run:
deno task dev      # http://localhost:3000
# or, production:
AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32) CANONICAL_ORIGIN=https://app.example.com \
  deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: cache-components
examples.title: Cache Components (use cache + PPR)
examples.blurb: A minimal demo of Next.js 16 Cache Components on denext, a stable opt-in enabled by top-level cacheComponents: true in denext.config.ts (Next.js's experimental: { cacheComponents: true } spelling…
examples.run:
deno task dev      # http://localhost:3000
# or
deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: caching
examples.title: caching — denext data cache & ISR
examples.blurb: Demonstrates denext's Next.js-compatible caching primitives, none of which had an example before.
examples.run:
# from this directory
deno task dev             # http://localhost:3000  (dev always renders fresh)
deno task build && deno task start   # ISR + data cache active

examples.name: capacitor-ci
examples.title: examples/capacitor-ci
examples.blurb: A GitHub Actions recipe for a denext app wrapped in Capacitor: every push is fingerprinted with denext mobile fingerprint, and ships over the air when the native layer is unchanged, or as signed…
examples.run:
denext mobile fingerprint                       # the fingerprint alone
denext mobile fingerprint --json > before.json  # every input, hashed
# …edit a native file, add a plugin…
denext mobile fingerprint --diff before.json    # what changed, and the verdict
denext mobile fingerprint --write               # embed it (idempotent)
denext ota manifest out --native-fingerprint auto --dir . --sign ota.key

examples.name: clerk
examples.title: examples/clerk — Clerk on denext: the web and Deno Desktop, written once
examples.blurb: One Next.js-style app, written the way Clerk's Next.js quickstart writes it, that signs in with Clerk on the web and in a Deno Desktop window, with tests against a Clerk development instance in test…
examples.run:
cd examples/clerk && deno install
deno task dev
deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: concurrency
examples.title: denext × concurrent rendering
examples.blurb: A runnable demo of denext's fiber concurrency — the things the earlier cooperative scheduler could not do: time-slicing and mid-flight interruption.
examples.run:
deno task example:concurrency          # build once, serve
deno task example:concurrency --dev    # rebuild on each request

examples.name: content-collections
examples.title: Content collections
examples.blurb: @denext/content-collections in one app: a small blog whose posts are typed Markdown and MDX files on disk.
examples.run: deno task dev          # http://localhost:3000 — the post list; /blog/<slug> for an entry

examples.name: desktop-kitchen-sink
examples.title: Desktop kitchen sink (every Deno Desktop capability, window-tested)
examples.blurb: A denext desktop app that turns on every shipped Deno Desktop capability and calls each one from the page, plus an automated window test that packages the app, launches it and asserts every result:…
examples.run:
deno task desktop            # export + open the window (denext's pinned runtime, Deno 2.9.7)
deno task desktop:package    # write scripts/package-*.ts from the scaffold, then package
deno task test:window        # package, launch and assert every check (exits 1 on a failure)
deno task test:window --no-package   # reuse the last builds in dist/ (and their update key)
deno task test:window --no-update    # skip the full-app update install / rollback launches

examples.name: drizzle
examples.title: Drizzle ORM on denext
examples.blurb: Typed SQL with Drizzle ORM over Deno's built-in node:sqlite — no native addon, no query engine.
examples.run:
deno task install   # deno install — resolves drizzle-orm + the better-sqlite3 shim
deno task dev        # http://localhost:3000   (or: deno task build && deno task start)

examples.name: effect
examples.title: denext migrate — Effect (Next app) fixture
examples.blurb: An actual Next.js App Router app that depends on Effect, used as the golden fixture for denext migrate's Effect support.
examples.run: deno run -A cli.ts migrate examples/effect

examples.name: effect-runtime
examples.title: denext + Effect — runnable bridge demo
examples.blurb: A minimal, runnable native-denext App Router app that runs Effect inside a Server Component via @denext/effect, showing:
examples.run: deno task dev     # http://localhost:3000

examples.name: expo-app
examples.title: Expo app in React Native mode (Capacitor)
examples.blurb: Expo's own starter, expo-template-default@57.0.27 (Expo SDK 57, the npm tarball sha512-E8P3+6k/6QNGKBZGw02/DachMMRUIT8MG0rXq8+N/J7EYZLO+rNH/0DZmDirU/Qwnj1zz6H40ySyS0AJmtZVBw==, 0BSD, see LICENSE),…
examples.run:
npm install --legacy-peer-deps   # the app's packages and the Capacitor shell's
deno task dev                    # the app in a browser: http://localhost:3000
deno task export                 # static export → out/ (Capacitor's webDir)
deno task cap:sync               # export + `cap sync ios`
DENEXT_IOS_TEAM=ABCDE12345 deno task ios   # a signed Debug build (xcodebuild)
deno task ios:check              # an unsigned compile check
deno task mobile:dev             # live reload on a phone: the shell loads `denext dev`

examples.name: fonts
examples.title: fonts — self-hosted Google fonts (next/font/google)
examples.blurb: A one-page app that loads a Google font through the next/font/google compat module and self-hosts it at build time — no runtime request to Google.
examples.run:
# from this directory
deno task dev             # http://localhost:3000  (runtime <link> fallback)
deno task build && deno task start   # fonts self-hosted from /_denext/fonts

examples.name: game
examples.title: denext × Three.js — "Rivet Rumble"
examples.blurb: A small 3D game built on Three.js (WebGL — plain JavaScript, not WASM) running on denext, bundled through the same next-compat esbuild path that handles motion / recharts.
examples.run:
deno task example:game          # build once, serve → http://localhost:3005
deno task example:game --dev    # rebuild on each request

examples.name: graphql
examples.title: examples/graphql
examples.blurb: @denext/graphql in one app: a Pothos (code-first, no decorators) schema served by GraphQL Yoga at /graphql, with a subscription that rides a denext channel — a post mutation publishes to…
examples.run: deno task dev          # http://localhost:3000 — GraphiQL at /graphql

examples.name: hello
examples.title: hello — the denext starter tour
examples.blurb: The smallest end-to-end denext app, and the one the docs and benchmarks lean on.

deno task start    # serve the build

examples.name: image

examples.name: live
examples.title: Live data & presence (secured)
examples.blurb: A runnable demo of the four gated Live hooks over a single WebSocket:
examples.run: deno task dev     # or: deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: mobile
examples.title: Mobile kitchen sink (Capacitor)
examples.blurb: A denext SPA in a Capacitor 8 shell that exercises every denext/mobile capability on one scrollable page: haptics, clipboard, share, device info, network, keep-awake, the splash screen, the secure…
examples.run:
npm install            # the Capacitor packages and plugins (package.json)
deno task dev          # the UI in a browser: http://localhost:3000
deno task build        # production build → .denext/
deno task export       # static export → out/ (Capacitor's webDir), stamped for OTA
deno task cap:sync     # export + `cap sync` into ios/ and android/
deno task mobile:dev   # live reload on a phone on the same Wi-Fi (denext mobile dev --lan)
DENEXT_IOS_TEAM=ABCDE12345 deno task ios   # a signed Release build (xcodebuild)

examples.name: native
examples.title: denext native example — desktop + mobile
examples.blurb: One denext app packaged three ways: the web, a native desktop app via deno desktop, and iOS / Android via Capacitor. All three serve the same static export (deno task export → out/).
examples.run:
deno task dev      # → http://localhost:3000
deno task start    # serve the production build

examples.name: native-views
examples.title: Native views in the layout (Capacitor)
examples.blurb: A denext SPA in a Capacitor 8 shell that puts native views inside a scrolling VirtualList: a map of London (row 3, placement="auto": embedded on iOS, drawn over the WebView on Android), a video…
examples.run:
npm install            # the Capacitor packages (package.json)
deno task dev          # the UI in a browser: http://localhost:3000
deno task cap:sync     # export + `cap sync` into ios/ and android/
DENEXT_IOS_TEAM=ABCDE12345 deno task ios   # a signed Debug build (xcodebuild)
deno task ios:check    # an unsigned compile check
deno task android      # android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

examples.name: next-compat
examples.title: next-compat example — real npm React libraries on denext
examples.blurb: This app renders the actual @radix-ui/react-collapsible npm package on denext's own React — server-rendered, then hydrated.
examples.run:
deno task example:next-compat          # build once, serve (production-like)
deno task example:next-compat --dev    # rebuild on each request

examples.name: next-compat-feasibility
examples.title: denext conversion feasibility — dependency validation
examples.blurb: Two probes that answer one question for a real Next.js app: would its dependency tree run on denext? They validate dependencies only — they do not convert the app.
examples.run:
# server deps (edit PACKAGES in the file to match the app)
deno run -A --node-modules-dir=auto examples/next-compat-feasibility/probe-server.ts

# client deps (run from the denext repo root; pass the app's root dir)
deno run -A --config deno.json examples/next-compat-feasibility/probe-client.ts /path/to/app

examples.name: next-compat-recharts
examples.title: next-compat: real recharts on denext (class components)
examples.blurb: This example runs the actual recharts npm package — a charting library built on React class components — on denext's single React, server-rendered to SVG and hydrated on the client.
examples.run:
deno task example:next-compat-recharts          # build once, serve (prod-like)
deno task example:next-compat-recharts --dev    # rebuild on each request

examples.name: notes
examples.title: examples/notes — a real, small denext app
examples.blurb: A notes app that answers "is this a toy?" in one read. It uses the pieces a real app needs, and every flow works with JavaScript disabled:

deno task dev      # http://localhost:3000
# or, production:
deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: openapi

examples.blurb: @denext/openapi in one app: a tiny pet store defined with defineApi + Zod, which the plugin turns — with no extra annotation — into an OpenAPI 3.1 document at /openapi.json, an interactive Swagger UI…

examples.name: pages-router
examples.title: pages-router — the @denext/pages-router plugin

deno task build && deno task start

examples.name: plugin-aliases
examples.title: denext plugin example: path aliases
examples.blurb: A ~40-line denext plugin — the smallest real one, and the first to use the route-synthesizer seam (@denext/pages-router uses the request-handler + build-step seams). See the plugin authoring guide.
examples.run:
cd examples/plugin-aliases
deno task dev            # http://localhost:3006

examples.name: postgres-load
examples.title: denext × Postgres under load
examples.blurb: The database guide says of networked databases: "these drivers are not part of denext's CI — validate your driver + pooling under your load." This example is that validation, made runnable.
examples.run:
cd examples/postgres-load
cp .env.example .env         # DATABASE_URL + POOL_SIZE

deno task db:up              # start Postgres in Docker (or point .env anywhere)
                             # it publishes 127.0.0.1:5432 — this machine only
deno task build              # build the app
deno task start              # serve on http://localhost:3005

examples.name: prisma
examples.title: Prisma ORM on denext
examples.blurb: The app is a tiny notes list: a Server Component awaits the Prisma query and renders the rows, and a native <form> posts a Server Action that inserts through the same Prisma client — no client…
examples.run:
deno task setup   # one-time: bundle the shim, install, prisma generate + db push
deno task dev      # http://localhost:3000   (or: deno task build && deno task start)

examples.name: react-router
examples.title: examples/react-router
examples.blurb: A React Router v7 framework-mode app running on denext through @denext/react-router, with the route components left unmodified — they still import { Outlet, Form, useLoaderData } from "react-router".
examples.run: deno task dev          # http://localhost:3000

examples.name: resumability
examples.title: Resumability demo
examples.blurb: A route rendered with export const resumable = true: interactive with no up-front hydration. Islands resume on demand — click one counter and only that island hydrates.

deno task dev          # the CLI prints the local URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000)
# or a production build:

examples.name: rn-desktop
examples.title: React Native on the desktop (reactNative + Deno Desktop)
examples.blurb: A React Native component tree (react-native-web) running in a Deno Desktop window, with native desktop capabilities: the counter persists in the OS keychain, right-click opens the native context…

npm install          # react-native-web (the app's own dependency; denext ships none)
deno task dev        # in the browser
deno task desktop    # export + open in a native window (Deno 2.9+)
deno task desktop:dev    # live reload inside the window
